def logs_error_total(rows):
    """Compute the aggregate unit total attributed to error records within a
    batch of normalized log rows.

    This routine forms part of the summarization stage of a log-processing
    pipeline. Upstream collectors gather event records from a fleet of
    services during a reporting window, normalize them into a fixed shape,
    and deliver them to this function as the argument rows. Each element of
    rows is a list of exactly three values: a name (str), a qty (int), and a
    unit (int). The name field identifies the category under which the
    originating collector filed the event, the qty field records a count
    carried through from the collection stage, and the unit field records
    the figure that downstream reporting consumes. Historically these
    records were assembled from raw text logs; the present normalized form
    was adopted so that summarization routines such as this one can operate
    without reference to the original log lines.

    For the purposes of the daily operations digest, only records filed
    under the error category are of interest here; records of every other
    category appear in the batch because the upstream stage delivers the
    full reporting window without pre-filtering. Return the sum of unit over
    the rows whose name is exactly the string 'error'. The resulting figure
    is written by the digest generator into its error-total field.

    Batches may arrive empty, for instance when a reporting window closes
    with no traffic recorded, and such input is regarded as ordinary rather
    than exceptional. The examples below illustrate the expected behavior on
    an empty batch and on a batch containing a single error record.

    >>> logs_error_total([])
    0
    >>> logs_error_total([['error', 41, 3]])
    3
    """
